documents.title: Typological Study On the Workplace Faith Fellowship In Its Three Stages of Historical Development in Korea
documents.abstract: I. INTRODUCTION A. Posing of Problem and the Task of Study The National Statistical Office reported that about 22,219,000 workers are employed nationwide by the September, 2002. This numeric reaches 46.6% of the whole population in Korea. Recent report says that workers feel discouraged and unsecured because of the hostile working environment, limitless competition, structural injustice of industrial society, economic and societal conflict between the rich and the poor, psychological stress and tension, collapse of family and virtue system, and, blurring of the ethical sensitivity in the workplace. It is not surprising therefore to hear from the groups of age in 20' and 30' complaining of their unstable job and future. 'For where two or three are gathered together in my name, I am there in the midst of them' (Mt. 18:20). So many believers have experienced hope and consolation from this text. The text gives not only psychological easiness but also Chris tian vision of vocation that the workplace is the one in which Christ's presence is to be experienced and witnessed. Workplace Faith Fellowship has been the place in which believers are exposed to the concrete real world and encouraged to create and participate in the mystical visible body of Christ, and called to share Christian life in a hostile real world of selfishness, competition, and injustice. It has challenged believers to live with honesty and responsibility the wholistic Christian life supposed to be accomplished through the interconnected structures of family, church, and work place. Considering of its original vision, however, future of the WF appears to be not so hopeful because of the accelerating process of secularization in society. For the writer devoting to the workplace ministry in the Holy Love Church Furniture Company last ten years, current situation is discouraging. How could I revitalize and realize the original vision of the workplace mission? How could I form the faith community in workplace in which believers are challenged to express and create their Christian identity? How could believers be more faithful to Christ's simple words like these: 'Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature' (Mark 16:15); 'You are the salt of the earth but if the salt loses its flavor, how shall it be seasoned? It is then good for nothing but to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by men' (Matthew 5:13). Task of the study is to characterize and evaluate the activities and influence of WFs by using four typologies the writer creates, that is, the worship-centered, the Bible study-centered, the mission-centered, and fellowship-centered, from theological and sociological perspectives, with its three stages of historical development in view. Motif of the study is to help members, leaders, prospective leaders of WF and church leadership confronting ones' history and thereby revitalizing their self-identity in a new way. B. Methodology and the Scope of the Study The study depends on literary analysis of diverse materials from WF and visitation. In Introduction, task and motif of the study will be revealed. Scope of study will be defined. In Chapter II, theoretical ground of WF will be laid, historically, theologically, and sociologically. Historical origins of three categories of WF especially in connection with its leadership style be introduced historically. Theological principles or assumptions of WF will be analyzed in terms of the nature of laity, stewardship, and mission of sending. In sociological analysis, the writer will deal with the value of vocation in diverse perspectives. Chapter III, IV and V deal with history of the WF in its three stages of development: the early (1950'-1970'), the middle (1980'-1990'), and the present (2000-present). Activities in each stage will be explored and characterized in four typologies: the worship centered, the Bible study centered, the mission centered, and the fellowship-diakonia centered, evaluated from theological and sociological perspective, and, summarized critically. II. Theoretical Reflection on Workplace Faith Fellowship A. Historical Reflection The writer analyzes the history of Korean WF in four typologies of the worship centered, the Bible Study Centered, mission centered, and fellowship centered. Four typologies are categorized in terms of the primary concerns and focuses of activities of diverse groups of WF. Though not adopted as a categorizing typology in the thesis, another perspective to categorize WFs would be worth being remarked. It is related to the question of leadership, that is, 'who takes initiative to run WF. 1. Independent Workplace Faith Fellowship Historical origin of WF is known to be a prayer meeting held in Dansung Sa (movie theater) run at that time by Byuksan Co. in 1956. Initiative of this meeting was taken by a devote Christian owner of Byuksan Co.. Theater was open to public on Sunday. And Christians of employees in the company couldn't attend Sunday Worship Service. The owner felt deeply sorry about this situation, finally decided to provide certain space and time (one of weekday) for employees to have opportunity to have service. Though not systematically organized and given space for more creative and extended activities compared to WF today, WF in Dansung Sa is a historical phenomena in Korean christian soil in which worship service celebrated in the church on Sunday is the normative considered biblical and therefore effective. Characteristic of this type of WF is that the owner of the company takes initiative and the activities are restricted more or less within that company. 2. Workplace Mission Association In the pluralistic secular city like Seoul, there are so many big companies, officially not affiliated to any religion. It is hard in this case to get any help for Christian activities from companies, for example. Under this circumstance, there comes up individual Christians, forming an areal christian network which could be called WF. Usually they ask churches in area to provide space and sometimes leadership for meeting. The meeting held at Chonkyo Methodist Church in 1979 is the one in this kind. They first called the meeting as 'Thursday workplace church' because they met at Thursday lunchtime. Members of this meeting introduced their activities around the area, invited other Christian workers to the Easter Service in 1980, and decided to develop 'Thursday workplace church' into 'Workplace Mission Association.' This type of WF has been established since then in big cities, now reaching the nationwide networking of 38 areal organizations by now. In this type of WF, leadership or the initiative is taken by christian workers' network voluntarily established, but with strong relationship with one church in the area who provides meeting space, financial support, and some part of leadership. 3. Workplace Church Worship Workplace Church Worship is a type of meeting in which a certain church takes full initiative in making organization, funding, and providing leadership. The meeting usually origins as a result of mission project of an urban church for the area. Youngrak Presbyterian church began this type of mission project September 5 1969. Church invited workers of Ssang Yong Cement, Bbaek general hospital, Jungbu police station and began worship service at lunch time every Friday. In this type of WP, leadership is under a local church. B. Theological Reflection 1. Theology of Laity Theological ground of WF appears to be theology of laity which is based on the doctrine of priesthood of believers reclaimed by Martin Luther. Luther argued that the only mediator is Jesus Christ and christians baptized have grace of privilege to participate in Christ's priesthood as his visible body in this world. This means that every christian has a duty and privilege to proclaim gospel and offer a prayer of intercession in every place and time, offering spiritual and living worship. Priesthood and apostolic right is not just restricted to the church institution (ordained clergy). Priesthood is to be reinterpreted and applied to all believers in Jesus Christ. The doctrine of priesthood of believers is the ground of the theology of laity and theological justification of WF. What is the biblical meaning of the term 'laity'? As 'laos,' in Greek, it indicates people of God including both clergy and believers not ordained. The term 'laity' is a glorious word because people of God is nothing other than a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people made to proclaim the mighty acts of him who call themselves out of darkness into his marvelous light (1 Peter 2:9). In the early stage of the Christian history, laity means community of believers including apostles, prophets, teachers, deacons, and others given diverse gifts from Holy Spirit, only later, coming to be degraded when it began to indicate a group of believers unordained, passive, derivative and secondary compared to the ordained in the mission of the church. Theology of laity based upon the doctrine of priesthood of believers appears to be implied or assumed in activities of WF. 2. Theology of Stewardship Another theological principle of workplace mission comes from Genesis 1: 28: 'have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the bird....' Message is about stewardship assigned and commanded to human being as image of God. Steward is the faithful and prudent manager (Luke 12:42), servants of Christ and steward of God's mysteries (1 Cor. 4:1), guardians and trustees, blameless (Gal. 4:2). To serve the world as Christ did is one of theological principles which could explain WF's activities in meaningful way. 3. Theology of 'Being Sent' Jesus Christ trained his disciples for three years, sending them to the world. In John 17:18 reading 'As you have sent me into the world, so I have sent them onto the world,' what we see is the special relationship among God, Jesus Christ and disciples, the relationship characterized as 'sending' and 'sent.' God sent Jesus and Jesus sent disciples. Message is about mission and the importance of the relation between the one who send and the one who is sent. Sender gives full authority to the one who is sent. The one to be sent represents the sender in full scale. Jesus also commands to his disciples just before ascension: 'Go therefore and make disciples of all nations' (Mt. 28:19). This command of mission is passed over to members of WF through the disciples. WF is community to be sent to make disciples by God in and through Jesus Christ in this world, that is, in workplace. Being sent is an important theological perspective to have members of WF see their vocation with responsibility and faith. C. Sociological Reflection Korean war (1950-1953) had devastated Korean economy. Poverty was the main issue and problem to be solved to any subsequent political leaderships thereafter. Since 1962 Korean government launched a grand project called '5 Year Economic Development Plan.' The first '5 Year Economic Development Plan' was accomplished during 1962-1966 and the fifth and the last one during 1977-1981. 25 years of national project to elevate economic standard brought rapid and dramatic economic development and prosperity on the one hand, however, moral hazard and loss of ethics of work on the other hand resulting in the IMF period (1997-19998). WF understands their workplace as a mission field and vocation as place in and through which one is called to the service of God and the world. This kind of highly ethical and theological perception of vocation in the consciousness of members of WF came to be known and valued in and out of WF in this one-dimensional wasteland of this kingdom of profit. III. The Initial Stage of Workplace Faith Fellowship (1950s-1980s) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. National Assembly Prayer Breakfast National Assembly Prayer Breakfast was begun in November 1965 by Christian members of the 6th National Assembly, led by Assemblywoman Hyun-Sook Park. The meeting was begun to better love brothers and sisters in Christ, to worship, and was started with the prayer that 'His will be done' in our nation 'as in Heaven.' In May of 1968, the National Assembly Prayer Breakfast and the Korean Prayer Breakfast Committees jointly established National Prayer Breakfast, an annual event where the President, prominent figures of the three departments of the government, and other leaders of different spheres of influence, gathered to pray. Those attending this Prayer Breakfast, despite their unique positions as members of the Assembly, approached the workplace with a firm sense of Christian duty, and the event sublimated into one in which true workplace worship occurred. Their main activity was their Prayer Breakfasts that were held on the first Wednesdays of each month at 7:30 am in the National Assembly Prayer Room (13206), during which the members held service and shared breakfast. They also held service on the days regular as well as extraordinary Assembly meetings were called to order. What is specially noteworthy is that even after the Christian members of the Assembly in opposing parties had confronted each other in fierce debates, they would always worship as one in Christ, giving honor to God and sharing love in fellowship with one another. 2. National Assembly Prayer Meetings National Assembly Prayer Meetings are a separate WF from National Assembly Breakfast Prayer. This WF had its start when three sisters in Christ (Kyung-Hae Kim, Young-Sook Choi, Chi-Myung Park) met to hold a prayer meeting on October 22, 1976. At the time, with no rooms available in which to have worship, the group of three met in storage rooms, ventilation room, or utility rooms to raise up earnest, tearful prayers. By God's provision they were able to hold their first meeting in their newly obtained permanent prayer room, in basement room 206, on September 12, 1979. The sound of prayer never ceased coming from this room for an entire year. On December 26 1979, the National Assembly Prayer Association's Inaugural General Synod (President: Chang-Lyul Kim) met, and on January 5th 1980 they held an Inaugural Worship Service Sermon: Bishop Gi-Chun Jang). B. Bible Study Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship As Bible study centered WF, Faith Movement for Bankers of the Bank of Korea can be pick up. It had its humble beginnings on August 27, 1975 with three people at the preparatory prayer meeting. On November 26 the same year, they had the Inaugural General Synod and began its growth as a WF. The regulation established at this time, 'We are to spread Biblically grounded Gospel, and in fostering interrelationship among members, give glory to God,' was the purpose of this ministry and now, 20 years after, the same holds. From March 20, 1978 four teams of 40 members committed to group Bible studies began. For those who may wonder, 'Why Bible studies at this particular time?', it could be said that the studies were prompted by the 'New Living' seminar that was started at Bank of We. At the time in 1978, over the course of four days of February 14th to the 17th at the 2nd meeting, an average of 350 people attended every day, making the Bank of Korea auditorium a place where many were touched. As an outflow of such memorable experience Bible study groups sprang up in different departments. As teaching material they used what Pastor Dong-Won Lee (Then Faith Movement for Bankers leader and Pastor of Global Missions Church) provided, 'The 9 Steps of the Creed.' The Bible studies span on average 30 to 40 minutes, and are divided into times of Bible study, prayer, fellowship, and praise. About 80% of the time is spent on the study of the Bible, which is also divided into Bible reading, teaching, and sharing, of which teaching is alloted 50% of the time. Outside the regular meetings, the Bible study members meet to visit and serve at centers for the disabled and senior citizens. They also collect money to celebrate special occasions such as birthdays and promotions, to give farewell gifts to those being transferred, and in addition, many groups jointly go on one day prayer retreats. C. Mission Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship The Missions Society of Seoul Bank is WF that was founded in the midst of much discord and hurt resulting from the merger between Seoul Bank and Sintak Bank in 1976. The group had its beginning as a seemingly inconsiderable prayer meeting. It was Jong-Bok Kim, then central staff member of CCC (Korea Campus Crusade for Christ)6), who had vision of having a group 'Centered ministering lay people at the workplace,' and to help foster the 'growth as a global bank' in order to 'share in the vision of world missions' which made the birth of this group, on January 1977, possible. In September of 1997, this small society grew to include 500 registered members with chapters in Busan, Jam-sil Jun-San Center, L.A., and developed to have different departments specializing in worship Service, evangelism, volunteering, pamphlet missions, and musical praise. To vitalize the regional chapters, advising pastors and/or officers are appointed to go and to take part in their worship services, partake in fellowship, and exchange information, particularly in order to discuss evangelism methods. Those from the main headquarters regularly attend meetings at the chapters and are jointly pushing for business missions. D. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Investment Firms Workplace Faith Fellowship At the starting point of the history of Korean WF, we find the Investment firm WF. On December 27; 1977, Christian employees working in investment firms with a united desire to spread the Gospel in their field established three independent WFs in the old National Theatre in Myoung Dong. The mission statement of the group was to foster the holy fellowship of believers in the realm of investment and to accomplish Jesus Christ's great missions commission. As they remained true to these founding principles and put them to action, the group now consists of 30 investment firms WFs with 3000 members spread over the country, including their four regional chapters in Busan, Gwang Joo, Ool San, and Dae Gu, and becomes an influential missions organization. 2. Youngrak Church's Workplace Church Worship Different from unit WFs with leadership taken by a particular WF and meeting held during the weekday, for workplace church worship type of WF, leadership is provided by the local church. This local church provides with leadership, fund, meeting place and other ones in need. This is immediately related to city church's mission strategy to reaching out surrounding regional community. This WP started by Youngnak Church (Senior Pastor: Chul-Shin Lee) located in Ju-Dong, Seoul, and also that first of its kind in Korea, celebrates its 35th anniversary in 2004. During lunch break of yet another ordinary Friday September 5th 1969, this kind of WF was offered to the workers in the area who were employed at places such as Ssang Young Cement, Bbaek General Hospital, and the Junbu Police Station. 10 people had attended the first worship service but at the present some 200 people have become regulars. E. Evaluation 1. Sociological and Theological Evaluation The economic state of Korea in its beginnings as a modern country was dismal. After the tragedy of the fratricidal Korean War, country faces a great hardship. Factories, buildings, railroads, and other facilities of value were all destroyed, and the toll on human life was tremendous. According to data from an organization, civilian casualties soared as high as 244, 663 for South Korea alone, higher for North Korea with 406,000 dead, with 303,212 missing, and 680,000 wounded or injured. No doubt, it was a period of great darkness. Notwithstanding, WF that was started in 1956 sublimated the deep hurts from the war with faith, and took on the great task of spreading the Gospel, and of serving society. When giving a theological (ecclesiological) evaluation of the WF in its early years, one should make it from the theological perspective of 'sending.' God is the subject of missions. God's mission began with the sending of His son Jesus Christ into this world, and the love that sent His only son was not limited to Israel or a certain nation but was meant for all of humanity. The theological perspective of 'sending' characterizes the nature of activities of WF in its initial stage of historical development. Also thanks to this theology the worship, service format centered on the leadership of minister gave way to that grounded upon the leadership of laity. This theology justifies the fact that worship could be brought out from the church building into the outside world. 2. Overall Evaluation It is worth noting that WF in its early stage was established out of the poor lay leaderships, inferior working environment in which general ethos is so opposite from that of Christian vision of living, and absence of more or less articulated theological ground. Namely, it would be likely that the most active minority are not in the mainstream in the workplace. This would probably result in WF's somewhat restricted influence on workplace or the society. Attempting to classify the various WFs from the early years, the writer suffers most because of rarity of materials answering questions like these: 'How many leaders were working?' 'how were they equipped with more technical knowledge,' 'how were new comers trained and nurtured?' 'how many people worked actively?' IV. The Middle Stage of the Workplace Faith Fellowship (1981-1990) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Sung-Ae Church Furniture Company Sung-Ae Church Furniture Company was founded on 1967. Company motto was 'Safely and Faithfully,' 'Diligently and Wisely,' 'Enduring Faith.' The company places priority on WF worship. In 1977, after the Sung-Ae Furniture Company Factory was rebuilt for expansion, Thanksgiving Service (sermon: Pastor Jung-Soo Park) was held. From this worship, the company's WF worship was decided to take on a new form as 'Monday Service,' with the purpose of offering the first hour of the workweek to God. Of course, there have been services at Sung-Ae from its founding, but it was in a form that merely followed class meeting order of Methodist Church. Main Activities focused on missions in and abroad, miscellaneous activities, which would actualize philosophy of management: 'Glory to God. 2. Ebenezer of Samsung Electronics Ebenezer is the name of WF in Samsung Electronics, an affiliated enterprise of Samsung Group, located in Gi-Heung of Kyoung-Gi Provence. It started when Chul Jin Lee (at present Professor of Nano Technology at Han Yang University), Kwang-Hee Yang, and a few other brothers met to hold worship services together in 1984. Main activities of this WF is as follow: regular meetings (Tuesdays every week at the women's dormitory Baek-Hap dong education center in basement, 6pm); prayer meetings at Paul Prayer Center; missions abroad Ebenezer retreat. 3. Christian Workplace Faith Fellowship of Seoul Subway Corporation The Christian WF of Seoul Subway Corporation held its initiation meeting on June 29, 1984, and held the Christian WF worship commemorating its founding September 15, 1984. They named the community as 'Christian WF of Seoul Subway Corporation,' and elected Han Mo Jung as president, and, celebrated its inaugural worship servide with Rev. B. Bible Study Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Business Bible Belt ('BBB') BBB had its beginning when around 40 workers in Myong Dong business area gathered together to study the Bible on January of 1990, to be trained and nurtured in faith, and to accomplish discipleship fully and effectively in workplace given to them. This has become an extensive organization. This WF has 1,300 participating members in cities of Seoul (areas of Myoung Dong, Gwang Hwa Moon, Seoul Station, Gang Nam, Yoido) and is active in other cities like Chun An, Dae Gu, Dae Jun, Ik San. BBB's strategy for mission is as follow: living out a life of evangelism in the workplace; establishing a small size of groups of Bible study; cultivating leadership; working together for spreading the Gospel. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. The United Korea Energies Workplace Faith Fellowship 'Heralds of Light, triumph over the darkness' (Korean hymnal. 259). E. Evaluation 1 Sociological and Theological Evaluation It would not be a stretch to say that phenomenal flourishing of Korea WFs in this middle period was a beneficiary of the impressive economic growth of the 1980s and 90s. After the Korean War, government adopted forceful economic policies, and accomplished amazing task which could be called 'the miracle of Han River.' Korea has been changed drastically from the agricultural nation to the highly developed industrial nation in this period. 2. General Evaluation WFs in this period were under the situation of astounding economic growth and development. It is to be noted, however, that economic growth brought about divisions and conflicts among the various groups of the economic classes. WF concerns this social conflicts in workplace. WFs were growing in number at this period. Yet along with this accomplishment we find that there are slight problems as well; surprisingly, there are no, and if any very few, cases of successful evangelization of non-believing co-workers in the company. It seems that the priorities had been shifted. It reminds me, as it is depicted in Acts 6:1-2, of how even those of the early church, after there was a great revival and masses became believers, found themselves in a situation where they were struggling with disunity in regards to relief work, as opposed to clinging harder to the most important things, that is, prayer and the Word: Now during those days, when the disciples were increasing in number, the Hellenists complained against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food. And the twelve called together the whole community of the disciples and said, 'It is not right that we should neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.(Acts 6:1-2) Similarly we can see in this period that WFs put more emphasis on the derivative elements rather than on the most important, which was the saving of souls in the workplace. In addition, I would like to point out that much of missions of WF in the workplace was accomplished under the lay leadership, meaning that there decreased a feeling of necessity of the existence of the ordained ministry for the workplace and of the connection between WFs and local churches. Being a time of many shortcomings, this period was also a time during which companies of the faith were founded, and in which lay leadership in ministry is awakened and flourished. I would call this period as 'the Miracle of WF.' V. The Present Stage of the Workplace Faith Fellowship (1991-present) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship On October 12, 2003, the staff workers of True Love Haven Fire Kiln Sauna, Sung Joon Jung and his family, and employees at the Jung Gun Public Company gathered for their first worship service together. They held their Inaugural Worship service on May 23, 2004, with Methodist District Superintendent Haang Sub Jin giving a sermon entitled 'A Desired Church.' The first regular worship service, its format taking after a conventional Sunday service, took place on October 12 with 20 people in attendance. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Workplace Faith Fellowship of National Correctional Facility WF of National Correctional Facility is community of the people who were called into the unique, and not easily accessible, ministry that gathered to form the National Correctional Facility Christian Fellowship. Like the disciples who were called in the most unlikely of places--under a fig tree, at the tax office, at the beach of Galilee, it is their belief that they, too, have been called forth as heralds of light. With God's calling through the verse ''I was in prison and you came to visit me.'' (Matthews 25:36), 2,000 correction officers take pride in the fact that they are missionaries at the edge, quietly carry on their task to serve wherever they are, and are putting in all their devotion to show that God's kingdom expands even into the prison cells. E. Evaluation 1. Sociological and Theological Evaluation Korea in the 1990s used the authoritarian model of development and experienced an unrivaled growth rate which placed it on 11th place in the world as a powerful international trading country, and in 1995 the country entered into the age of 1 million dollar GNP (at the time it was 9,000,000 won), allowing them to become an OECD member in 1996, which all in turn, made this member of the Four Asian Dragons a subject of research as a model of 3rd world development. Yet on January 23, 1997, the bankruptcy of Han-Bo Steel Company and the downfall of foreign credit rating marked the beginning of a chain of events such as an insolvency postponement agreement, peace talks, court receivership, continued falling of stock and rising exchange rates, and the depletion of usable foreign currency reserves of the Korean bank, led to an official request to the IMF for a rescue loan on December 3, 1997, and as a result of the financial panic after the completion of the rescue loan agreement with the IMF, the economy recession worsened, leaving the country overall in a dire economic crisis. Yet despite the turbulence of going from one economic extreme to another, the National Christian Workplace Mission Council of the 90s, by continuing its organizational expansion into 31 regions to successfully form a national structure, showed a certain systemized strength. In fact, as the members of WFs played their part during the national crisis, the group showed its potential. In this crisis, theological implication of stewardship has played an important role to shape WF's self identity. 2. Overall Evaluation The Korean WFs of this period can be described with 'diversity,' in form as well as in workplaces in which they are founded. From the beginning of the late 90s, responding to what could fairly be termed as a new craze for workplace missions, new mission societies have been formed. The representative organization is the 'Korean Christian Workplace Mission Clergy Association ('KWC').' This association was founded on September 28, 1998 by the ministers of this country's mainstream denominations. KWC and 'Korean Christian Workplace Mission Association,' sharing the same office, expressing their cooperation for mission, still have fundamental differences in the makeup one is for pastors, and the other for laity. The forming of the KWC suggests in some way that the clergy are actively entering into workplace missions. Another problem is the inferior research situation. There is a lack of interest among churches, denominations, seminaries and ministers in this field, not to mention research. This situation is reflected on the publication of books on this subject. Hong-Il Park's book, Workplace Missions and Site of Life was published on February of 2000, and Theology of Mission in Workplace,' authored by Kyung Won Kim, Dong Yoon Jun, and Sang Gi Jun, was published as late as September of 2001. Needless to say, there is an extreme lack of dissertations and research work as well as educational material written on this topic. Within the church, too, education provided for workers is not readily available, not continuous, or systematized. Yet devotion and effort shown by the various WFs deserve acknowledgement and compliments. It is my analysis that these WFs provided great encouragement to Korean workers and Korean citizens overall who were suffering under unprecedented national hardship during IMF period. VI. Conclusion Questions driving the writer last ten year in his double ministries both in the local church and workplace setting are like these: 'Why am I so eagerly involved in the ministry for the workplace along with the ministry for local church?'; 'How could the 'AT help members living faithfully their Christian life in the real life of the workplace?' The writer has revealed, analyzed and evaluated the activities and influence of the WF in four typologies following three stages of historical development with sociological and theological perspective in view. And the thesis intends to be an answer to those questions. One of recent statistics shows that many of workers aged twenty to thirty supposed to be dressed up with excitement and vision, however, feel unsecured in their workplace owing to the threatening situation of economic depression in the larger context and discharge in the small context. It is a symbolic indication of the hard reality of life condition to get through in Korea. Workplace is the one in which the secular and Christian faith is clashed, Christian faith is supposed to take reality, and, the meaning of faith continued to be questioned and deepened in concrete way. WF is the community gathered in the name of Jesus Christ right in this heart of secular section, based on the biblical phrase: 'Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them' (Mt. 18:20), thereby witnessing Lord's presence and its salvafic implications for the people's lives in the workplace. It has been the place in which workers of Christian faith is given hope, encouragement and calling experience. Especially calling experience such that God works through me in this place or God brought me here appears to be the background of ethical and spiritual reading of secular vocation and workplace. It has been the place in which all the Christian members are brought and transfigured into one body of Christ, sharing brotherhood and sisterhood, and, breaking sorrow and joy of life together. Study characterizes WF as a source of spiritual power to help members overcoming duality of faith and life, family and workplace, worship and secular vocation to the maturity of more comprehensive Christian life, defining those effects an important contribution WF made for the Korean church and society. Thesis characterizes activities of WF in four typologies of the worship-centered, the Bible study-centered, mission-centered, and fellowship-centered, and, evaluates each typology from theological and sociological dimension with historical background in view. In chapter II, the writer presents theoretical ground of WF in terms of its historical, theological, and, sociological aspect. Historically, three types of WF were introduced. They are categorized by the nature of leadership: 'Independent WF,' the first Christian meeting held in workplace, 'Workplace Mission Association,' and 'Work Place Church Worship.' Theologically the self identity and activities of these groups in the early stage reflect theology of laity nurtured by the doctrine of priesthood of believers, devotional stewardship, and missiological vision Jesus exemplified in his training and sending of disciples. Sociologically, the writer shows how theses groups adapt themselves in the rapid societal change during 25 years of 'The Five Year Economic Development Plan' designed and led by government. In chapter III, the writer deals with the period beginning from the time of establishment of 'Korean WF' ending up to 1980 when the sequence of several '5 Year Economic Development Project' was closed. Groups are categorized in four and evaluated in its theological and sociological aspect: Worship Centered WF (Congressman's Breakfast Prayer Meeting-1965, Congress Prayer Meeting-1976) Bible Study Centered WF (Korean Bank Mission-1975) Mission Centered WF (Seoul Bank Mission-1977) Fellowship and Social Service Centered WF (Stock Committee Mission-1977). It is evident that groups of this period especially refer to theology of sending for their self identity. In chapter IV, the writer presents several groups belonging to the middle stage covering from 1980 to 1990. WFs in Korea reaches its golden age with the emergence of 'Christian Work Place Mission Council.' Groups are categorized in four and evaluated in its theological and sociological aspect: Worship Centered WF (Sacred Love Church Furniture-1984, Ebenesel WF-1984, Seoul Metropolitan Subway Co. WF-1984), Bible Study Centered WF ('BBB' meaning Business Bible Belt), Mission Centered WF which shows new pattern of workplace mission (City of Incheon WF Association-1988, City of Yeosou WF Association-1984, City of Daegu and Kyoungbuk WF Association-1990, City of Chuncheon WF Association-1990, City of Ulgin Nuclear Power Station WF-1985), Fellowship and Social Service Centered WF (Korean Electronic Co. WF-1989, Korean Drivers' Association-1985). Their activities appears to be grounded upon the theology of laity. In chapter V, the writer presents relatively recent activities of WF. After several decades of individual or corporative activities of WF, there established a 'Korean WF Mission General Council' for more mutual encouragement, exchange of information, and effective mission task. It was remarkable event in the history of workplace mission in Korea. Furthermore this insitution was registered as a corporation aggregate in the Ministry of Culture & Tourism. Groups are categorized in four and evaluated in its theological and sociological aspect: Worship Centered WF (True Love Shelter-2003), Bible Study Centered WFs which use Bible study text produced by NLTC (New Life Training Camp), Mission Centered WF (Korean Government Employee WF Association-1998, Ministry of Finance and Economy WF Association-1994), and, Fellowship and Social Service Centered WF (Korean Correctional Institution WF Association-1992). Their activities appears to be grounded upon the theology of stewardship. The writer attempts to introduce the hidden activities and stories of WF which has exercised positive influence on all sides of lives of Christian families, churches in Korea and of Korean society. They worked voluntarily with resolution. They lighted a candle of love in the darkness of workplace where competition, conspiracy, and hatred predominates, and, proclaimed the Sacred in the cement buildings of modern secular cities. To reveal their devotion, activities and theology itself would be a contribution to Korean churches in general. Churches always emphasize living worship, but not provides structures and leadership for living worship. All kinds of WF function to bridge church and life. Study attempts to cover all kinds of WF activities in full scale. But it was not easy to get all the official informations from WF. WF did not have an office to store the documents nor payed administrative leadership. Making and storing documents were not their primary concern. There might be still so many groups in workplace whose activities are not captured within writer's view. That might be the limit of the study. But if there is still something consoling the writer, it is the fact that there has been not one attempt to categorize WF movement periodically and typologically and to evaluate it with historical, theological, and sociological perspective.

documents.title: Big data를 이용한 Warehouse Management System 모델 연구 : SAP S/4 Hana를 중심으로
documents.abstract: 본 연구는 오늘날 산업 전반적으로 영향을 미치고 있는 디지탈 전환(Digital Transformation)의 기술 환경과 디지탈 전환의 산업적 창고관리 부분의 모델연구가 본 논문의 목적이다. &#xD; &#xD; 디지털 전환은 오랫동안 디지털화와 비슷하거나 또는 디지털 방식으로 저장할 수 있도록 기존 데이터 형태를 전환하는 것과 관련이 있다. 물론 이 점이 중요하긴 하지만, 이전의 디지털화는 최신 디지털 전환의 영역을 포함하지 않았었다.&#xD; &#xD; 특히 이번 연구에서는 Big Data를 중심으로 Warehouse Management System의 방향을 제시 하고자 한다.
documents.author: 이성훈

documents.title: DTG 실 주행데이터 및 공간정보를 이용한 빅데이터 기반 연료소모량 추정 모델 연구
documents.abstract: 한국에서 교통사고를 줄이는 목적으로 디지털운행기록계(DTG) 장치가 모든 상용차량에 의무 장착이 되어 GPS 궤적을 포함한 많은 양의 운행기록 데이터가 생성되고 있다. 지금까지 이러한 DTG 데이터는 주로 교통안전운전을 유도하는 용도로 사용되어왔다. 그러나 DTG데이터는 연료소모량을 줄일 수 있는 에코드라이빙 분야 등 다양한 분야로 활용도를 확대할 수 있다. 본 연구는 실제 운행한 대규모 DTG운행 데이터를 공간 빅데이터 분석을 통해 연료소모량을 추정할 수 있는 모델을 수립하는 연구이다. 기존의 연료소모량 추정 모델은 주로 실험실 환경 또는 일부 지역에 국한되어 검증한 모델로 실제 운행되는 상용차량 대상으로 분석할 경우 수집하기 어려운 변수들이 많고, 한국의 전국을 운행한 다양한 운행기록 데이터를 적용하면 정확도가 낮아지는 문제점이 있다. 본 연구에서는 이러한 문제를 개선하기 위해 DTG데이터와 공간 빅데이터를 이용한 연료소모량 추정 모델인 SBiFEM(Spatial Big Data Fuel Estimation Model)을 제안하였다. SBiFEM은 운전자 운행특성 및 도로의 다양한 환경정보를 반영하기 위해 운행 패턴과 공간 빅데이터 맵매칭 기술을 이용해 다양한 도로정보들을 입력변수로 추가 활용하는 분석 방법이다. 본 연구에서는 전처리, 공간빅데이터, 운행 패턴 생성에 이르는 전 과정에서 빅데이터 Map Reduce를 활용하는 공간빅데이터 분석 프로세스를 다음과 같이 수립하고 구현, 검증을 하였다. 첫째로, 전처리 기술 고도화이다. 센싱 데이터 및 GPS공간데이터 특성상 많은 양의 이상치 데이터(Outlier)가 존재하고 있어 이를 정제하지 않으면 분석결과도 신뢰할 수 없다. 이를 위해 통계기법 및 운행 패턴 분석을 이용한 필터링 기법을 연구하였다. 둘째로, 대량의 GPS궤적 데이터를 이용한 공간빅데이터 분석 체계이다. 차량 이동 데이터를 분석하기 위해서는 차량이 어느 도로에 위치 했는지를 알기 위한 전자지도와 매칭하는 맵매칭 기술이 필수적이다. 대부분의 맵매칭 기술은 실시간 내비게이션 용도로 주로 사용되어왔기 때문에 빠른 분석 속도를 요하는 빅데이터 분석에 적합하지 않다. 본 연구에서는 대량의 GPS궤적데이터를 전자지도에 매칭하는 빅데이터 맵매칭 기술을 연구하였다. 셋째로, 연료소모량을 추정하는 모델이다. 기존 추정 모델과의 차별점은 실제 운행환경을 반영하기 위한 변수들을 추가했다는 것이다. 한 종류는 차량 운행특성을 반영하는 운행 패턴이고, 또 한 종류는 전국의 다양한 도로 환경 정보이다. 이러한 도로 환경정보를 반영하기 위해 맵매칭 공간빅데이터 프로세스를 이용하였다.  SBiFEM 빅데이터 분석시스템 테스트 및 검증은 5대의 분산 서버에 Hadoop, HBase와 Map Reduce프로그램을 수행하여 성능 검증을 하였다. 또한 연료소모량 추정 모델 검증은 대표적인 연료소모량 및 배출가스 추정 모델인 SIDRA, VSP, VT-Micro등을 DTG데이터를 적용하여 분석한 결과와 본 연구의 모델을 적용한 결과를 비교하여 검증하였다. 비교결과 추정 값과 실제 값을 비교한 Correlation이 0.9169, MAPE(평균절대백분비오차)가 0.1846으로 본 연구의 모델 적용시 가장 우수하게 나와 본 논문에서 개발한 모델의 우수성을 검증하였다.
documents.author: 조원희

documents.title: Keynote speech 6: Big Data, IoT and the 2nd sustainable development goal
documents.abstract: The risks associated with the global food system are widely acknowledged and implicate a complex nexus of factors including increasing population, changing diets, erosion of natural capital, uncertain future climate, food price fluctuations, growing economic disparity and differential access to sufficient safe and nutritious food. The second sustainable development goal (SDG2) aims to address these challenges in every country to ensure not only that we eradicate global hunger, but also that everyone has access to safe and nutritious food that is produced in an environmentally, socially and economically sustainable manner. SDG2 creates an unprecedented challenge to overcome the complexity of coordinating interventions that span the whole food chain (more accurately, `food network') and engage a bewildering breadth of individuals, stakeholders and agencies. The Sustainable Development Solutions Network recommends a generic enabling framework for SDG2 that connects the various stakeholders, and indicates the feedbacks and information flows that are needed to ensure effective execution. This platform is broadly relevant to all countries irrespective of their development status. A clear requirement for the success of this framework is the availability and free exchange of data, together with near real-time analytics on that data to create the necessary knowledge flows. The potential role of data-driven innovation in implementing the enabling framework in developing and western economies will be discussed using various case studies. The opportunities for deploying existing and new kinds of sensor and networking technologies will be explored. This will include the potential role of IoT and Big Data related technologies and an evaluation of the feasibilities and risks associated with their deployment. The presentation will conclude with a set of requirements and a summary of recommendations for future priorities.
documents.author: Crawford, John

documents.title: Artificial intelligence and Big Data in neurology
documents.abstract:
ABSTRACT

Recent advances in technology have allowed us access to a multitude of datasets pertaining to various dimensions in neurology. Together with the enormous opportunities, we also face challenges related to data quality, ethics and intrinsic difficulties related to the application of data science in healthcare. In this article we will describe the main advances in the field of artificial intelligence and Big Data applied to neurology with a focus on neurosciences based on medical images. Real-World Data (RWD) and analytics related to large volumes of information will be described as well as some of the most relevant scientific initiatives at the time of this writing.
documents.author: Amaro Junior, Edson

documents.title: Big Data, Big Waste? A Reflection on the Environmental Sustainability of Big Data Initiatives
documents.abstract: This paper addresses a problem that has so far been neglected by scholars investigating the ethics of Big Data and policy makers: that is the ethical implications of Big Data initiatives’ environmental impact. Building on literature in environmental studies, cultural studies and Science and Technology Studies, the article draws attention to the physical presence of data, the material configuration of digital service, and the space occupied by data. It then explains how this material and situated character of data raises questions concerning the ethics of the increasingly fashionable Big Data discourses. It argues that attention should be paid to (1) the vocabulary currently used when discussing the governance of data initiatives; (2) the internal tension between current data initiatives and environmental policies; (3) issues of fair distribution. The article explains how taking into account these aspects would allow for a more responsible behaviour in the context of data storage and production.

documents.title: Enjeux des big data en santé
documents.abstract:
Summary

The government has commissioned a report on the topic, the Estates General on Bioethics refer to it and the Order of Doctors have published a white paper. Everybody is talking about big data and artificial intelligence but few have witnessed these innovations at work, innovations which now seem to be within reach of health professionals. This field, unknown to the general public a few years ago, has become an object of all fantasies and is bringing about a new industrial revolution.
documents.author: Cynober, Timoth&eacute

documents.title: Data learning from big data
documents.abstract:
Abstract

Technology is generating a huge and growing availability of observations of diverse nature. This big data is placing data learning as a central scientific discipline. It includes collection, storage, preprocessing, visualization and, essentially, statistical analysis of enormous batches of data. In this paper, we discuss the role of statistics regarding some of the issues raised by big data in this new paradigm and also propose the name of data learning to describe all the activities that allow to obtain relevant knowledge from this new source of information.

documents.title: 빅데이터 처리 프로세스에 따른 빅데이터 위험요인 분석
documents.abstract: Recently, as value for practical use of big data is evaluated, companies and organizations that create benefit and profit are gradually increasing with application of big data. But specifical and theoretical study about possible risk factors as introduction of big data is not being conducted. Accordingly, the study extracts the possible risk factors as introduction of big data based on literature reviews and classifies according to big data processing, data collection, data storage, data analysis, analysis data visualization and application. Also, the risk factors have order of priority according to the degree of risk from the survey of experts. This study will make a chance that can avoid risks by bid data processing and preparation for risks in order of dangerous grades of risk.
documents.author: 이지은;김창재;이남용;

documents.title: Big Data, Big Knowledge: Big Data for Personalized Healthcare
documents.abstract: The idea that the purely phenomenological knowledge that we can extract by analyzing large amounts of data can be useful in healthcare seems to contradict the desire of VPH researchers to build detailed mechanistic models for individual patients. But in practice no model is ever entirely phenomenological or entirely mechanistic. We propose in this position paper that big data analytics can be successfully combined with VPH technologies to produce robust and effective in silico medicine solutions. In order to do this, big data technologies must be further developed to cope with some specific requirements that emerge from this application. Such requirements are: working with sensitive data; analytics of complex and heterogeneous data spaces, including nontextual information; distributed data management under security and performance constraints; specialized analytics to integrate bioinformatics and systems biology information with clinical observations at tissue, organ and organisms scales; and specialized analytics to define the “physiological envelope” during the daily life of each patient. These domain-specific requirements suggest a need for targeted funding, in which big data technologies for in silico medicine becomes the research priority.
documents.author: Viceconti, Marco;Hunter, Peter;Hose, Rod;

documents.title: Big Data 활용을 위한 제조 품질 개선 방법에 대한 연구
documents.abstract: 20세기 대량 생산 시대 이래로 제조 기업의 품질은 가장 중요한 요소가 되어왔다. 따라서 품질에 대한 올바른 정의와 품질 개선을 위한 다양한 도구와 방법이 개발되어 왔으며 이의 효율적 적용을 위한 노력도 병행되어 왔다. 이러한 노력은 제조 기업의 품질 제일주의, 전사적 품질 경영, 식스 시그마 등을 통하여 정형화되고 다양한 분야에 적용되고 있다. 또한 최근 Big Data의 유용성이 소개되면서 이에 대한 제조 업계의 관심이 높아지고 있으나 이에 대한 적용은 아직 미흡한 면이 있다. 본 논문은 기존의 품질 개선을 위한 프로젝트 실행 방법을 정리해 보고 대표적인 프로젝트 중심의 개선 방법인 식스 시그마의 실행 방법을 기준으로 Big Data 활용 방법을 제안해 보기로 한다.

documents.title: BIG6 모형을 적용한 국어과 도서관협력수업이 정보활용 태도에 미치는 영향
documents.abstract: 학교도서관의 도서관협력수업은 학생들의 정보활용 교육을 위한 교육과정 운영을 위한 필수적인 기관으로 그 중요성이 강조된다. 본 연구에서는 여러 가지 정보 활용 모형 중 전 세계적으로 가장 널리 적용되고, 수준에 따라서 적용할 수 있도록 구분하고 있는 BIG6 모형을 적용한 교과목과 협력 수업을 통해 교수-학습장으로서 학교도서관의 이용을 증진시키고, 학생들 스스로 과제해결의 방법을 찾고, 이를 수업에 잘 적용할 수 있도록 하여 정보활용 능력을 신장시키고자 함에 목적이 있다. 문제해결 모형 BIG6 모형을 적용한 정보활용 수업이 학생들의 정보활용 태도에 미치는 영향을 미치는가를 연구하기 위하여 교수-학습안을 구안하여 수업을 실시한 후, 사전-사후 정보활용태도 검사를 실시하여 중학교 학생들의 정보활용 태도에 미치는 영향에 대하여 검증하였다. 교수-학습안은 중학교 2학년을 대상으로 생활국어를 중심으로 BIG6모형에서 제시하는 문제 해결 과정을 통해 학생들의 자기주도적으로 도서관의 자원을 활용하여 해결할 수 있도록 구안하였으며, 수업 진행은 교과교사와 사서교사간의 협의를 통해 진행되었다. 실험 대상은 중학교 2학년 4개반 154명을 대상으로 하였으며, 한 모둠에 5∼6명씩 협동으로 과제를 해결하고 조합하여 발표를 하는 방식으로 모둠학습을 진행하였다. 이를 통해 학생들의 '정보에 대한 탐색, 접근능력' 및 '정보의 분석, 이해능력', '정보의 종합, 적용 능력', '정보의 표현, 전달 능력', '정보 평가능력'등의 5가지의 정보활용 태도를 정보활용수업의 사전과 사후 설문을 통해 분석한 결과는 다음과 같다. 첫째, Big모형을 적용한 정보활용수업은 수업을 실시하기 전보다 수업 후의 학생들의 정보에 대한 탐색, 접근 능력 및'정보에 대한 탐색, 접근능력' 및 '정보의 분석, 이해능력', '정보의 종합, 적용 능력', '정보의 표현, 전달 능력', '정보 평가능력'등이 의미있게 향상된 것으로 학생들의 정보활용 태도에 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타났다. 둘째, Big모형을 적용한 정보활용수업을 실시하기 전보다 수업 후의 도서관의 이용 빈도 및 도서 대출횟수가 늘어나고, 도서관 정보활용수업의 태도에 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타났다. 본 연구의 결과 BIG6모형을 적용한 정보활용수업이 학생들의 정보활용태도를 향상 시키고, 도서관의 이용 빈도 및 자료이용을 향상시키는 것으로 나타났다. 본 연구결과는 다음과 같은 연구의 필요성을 제언한다. 첫째, 본 연구의 수업이 단기간 진행되었음에도 불구하고 전반적으로 정보활용태도의 향상이 되었다는 것은 이러한 수업이 장기적으로 이루어졌을 경우의 학생들의 정보활용 태도 및 정보이용 행태에 대한 연구가 계속 필요하다. 둘째, 본 연구에서 BIG6모형 과정을 기반으로 정보활용수업을 수행함으로써 학생들의 다양한 자료를 통한 자기주도적이며 창의적인 과제해결능력 향상 시킴으로써, 정보활용에 있어서 다양한 측면의 연구가 이루어질 필요가 있다.
documents.author: 양현정

documents.title: 칸트의 첫째 이율배반과 대폭발 우주론
documents.abstract: In this paper I studied Kant's first antinomy in connection with Big Bang Cosmology as a modern scientific cosmology. In this paper I assumed that the beginning of the universe in Big Bang Cosmology is the absolute beginning and that the universe is the total universe. The main argument is on the possibility or impossibility of the construction of Kant's first antinomy. By this argument I manifested which space-time Kant's first antinomy is based on. By this manifestation we can comprehend Kant's first antinomy more deeply, I am sure. I showed how Kant's first antinomy can be constructed when the argument concerning the spatial and temporal magnitude of the universe is based on Newtonian space-time. I argued that the construction of Kant's first antinomy is not possible concerning the spatial and temporal magnitude of the universe, in Big Bang Cosmology constructed by the notion of relativistic space-time.For those arguments, first of all I studied important notions, namely, space and time in Kant's first antinomy. Kantian space-time in the first antinomy is subjective representation, not substance. But I argued that in all the other properties of space-time Kantian space-time is the same as Newtonian space-time, and that Newtonian space-time exists independent of the universe.According to the notion of Newtonian space-time, the spatial and temporal magnitude of the universe is different from the magnitude of space-time existing as the background of the universe, and it is possible that in the infinite space-time there is partly the distribution of matter and partly a universe. Those make the construction of Kant's first antinomy possible from the viewpoint of transcendental idealism, I demonstrated.In Big Bang Cosmology constructed by the notion of relativistic space-time, space-time is determined by the distribution of matter. Therefore there is no space-time unrelated to the distribution of matter, and there can not be other space-time as the background of the universe than the space-time of the universe. Also there can not be the universe that have the distribution of matter partly in space-time. On the basis of those arguments, I demonstrated that Kant's first antinomy can not be constructed concerning the universe in Big Bang Cosmology constructed by the notion of relativistic space-time.Finally I argued that we can give the philosophical meaning to Kant's first antinomy on the notion of Newtonian space-time, and that we can't give the philosophical meaning to Kant's first antinomy in Big Bang Cosmology. However, if the beginning of the universe in Big Bang Cosmology is not the absolute beginning and the universe is not the total universe, we can give the philosophical meaning to Kant's first antinomy in Big Bang Cosmology, I argued.
documents.author: 곽윤항

documents.title: Efficient Dictionary Compression for Processing RDF Big Data Using Google BigQuery
documents.abstract: The Resource Description Framework (RDF) data model, is used on the Web to express billions of structured statements in a wide range of topics, including government, publications, life sciences, etc. Consequently, processing and storing this data requires the provision of high specification systems, both in terms of storage and computational capabilities. On the other hand, cloud-based big data services such as Google BigQuery can be used to store and query this data without any upfront investment. Google BigQuery pricing is based on the size of the data being stored or queried, but given that RDF statements contain long Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs), the cost of query and storage of RDF big data can increase rapidly. In this paper we present and evaluate a novel and efficient dictionary compression algorithm which is faster, generates small dictionaries that can fit in memory and results in better compression rate when compared with other large scale RDF dictionary compression. Consequently, our algorithm also reduces the BigQuery storage and query cost.

documents.title: Big data, oriented-organizational culture, and business performance: A socio-technical approach
documents.abstract: This paper experimentally examines the impact of oriented-organizational culture that could support big data analytics (BDA) in higher education institutions (HEIs) in Saudi Arabia. Specifically, this study analyzed the effect of oriented-organizational culture (OC) on big data tasks (BDTs) toward improving decision-making (DM) and organization performance (OP). The study hinged on the theory of socio-technical systems to investigate BDA elements in higher education decision-making in Saudi Arabia. The analysis was conducted using a quantitative survey research design where data were collected from 270 IT staff working in Saudi Arabian HEIs using Qualtrics. PLS-SEM was applied to validate the research data and explore the relationship between the proposed hypotheses. The findings show that oriented-organizational culture positively affected big data tasks, i.e., storing, analyzing, and visualizing. Similarly, oriented-organizational culture positively affects improving decision-making by top management in Saudi Arabian universities. OC also positively influences the performance of Saudi Arabian universities. Improving decision-making by top management has a positive impact on enhancing the overall university’s performance. However, big data tasks, i.e., storing, analyzing, and visualizing, negatively affect improving decision-making by top management in Saudi Arabian HEIs. One of the study limitations is the small sample size; future studies should include private and public universities to alter the expected outcomes. Additional technological elements, such as IT infrastructure at Saudi Arabia’s private and public HEIs, are recommended to be considered in future studies to establish the competence of respective IT infrastructure. AcknowledgmentThe authors wish to thank the Problems and Perspectives in Management Journal editors for their valuable time and assistance in improving the manuscript.
documents.author: Aseeri, Maher;Kang, Kyeong;

documents.title: Socio-technical factors influencing big data analytics adoption in healthcare
documents.abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the key socio-technical factors influencing big data analytics adoption in healthcare services. A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed scholarly publications spanning from 2013 to 2023 to illuminate the influencing factors. Twelve papers focused on the factors influencing big data analytics (BDA) adoption in healthcare services were included for review. The factors were divided into four major groups namely i) person, ii) technology, iii) organization, and iv) environment. Analytical skills define a person, whereas technology is characterized by system quality and information quality. Organization support, organization resources, training, data governance, and evidence-based decision-making are all associated with the organization. Finally, government regulations are allocated to the environment. This review presents evidence of the socio-technical factors that influence big data analytics adoption in healthcare services. The findings from this review recommend future big data analytics adoption in healthcare services to carefully evaluate the factors identified in this study.
documents.author: Wolseley, Nik Nurdini;Salahuddin, Lizawati;Mohd Aboobaider, Burhanuddin;Raja Ikram, Raja Rina;Hashim, Ummi Rabaah;Abdul Rahim, Fiza;

documents.title: Big data analytics on large-scale socio-technical software engineering archives
documents.abstract: Given the fast growing nature of software engineering data in online software repositories and open source communities, it would be helpful to analyse these assets to discover valuable information about the software engineering development process and other related data. Big Data Analytics (BDA) techniques and frameworks can be applied on these data resources to achieve a high-performance and relevant data collection and analysis. Software engineering is a socio-technical process which needs development team collaboration and technical knowledge to develop a high-quality application. GitHub, as an online social coding foundation, contains valuable information about the software engineers' communications and project life cycles. In this paper, unsupervised data mining techniques are applied on the data collected by general Big Data approaches to analyse GitHub projects, source codes and interactions. Source codes and projects are clustered using features and metrics derived from historical data in repositories, object oriented programming metrics and the influences of developers on source codes.

documents.abstract: This study examines changing public perceptions regarding South Korea’s power transmission grids (2000–2024) by using big data analysis and the socio-technical energy transition framework. By dividing the timeline around the Miryang incident (2012–2014), a pivotal protest against high-voltage towers, the study reveals a shift from viewing grids as technical systems to perceiving them as socio-technical infrastructures. Key trends include AC-to-DC transition, integration of renewables, and rising demands for transparency. These findings provide a framework for understanding long-term shifts in energy infrastructure perception and emphasize the importance of social factors in shaping effective energy transition policies.
documents.author: 김도형;선휘일;강송희;

documents.title: Ecological views of big data: Perspectives and issues
documents.abstract: From the viewpoint of big data as a socio-technical phenomenon, this study examines the associated assumptions and biases critically and contextually. The research analyzes the big data phenomenon from a socio-technical systems theory perspective: cultural, technological, and scholarly phenomena that rest on the interplay of technology, analysis, and mythology provoking extensive utopian and dystopian rhetoric. It examines the development of big data by reviewing this theory, identifying key components of the big data ecosystem, and explaining how these components are likely to evolve over time. Despite extensive investment and proactive drive, uncertainty exists concerning the evolution of big data and the impact on the new information milieu. Significant concerns recently addressed are in the areas of privacy, data quality, access, curation, preservation, and use. This study provides insight into these challenges and opportunities through the lens of a socio-technical analysis of big data development, which includes social dynamics, political discourse, and technological choices inherent in the design and development of next-generation ICT ecology. The policy implications of big data are addressed using Korean information initiatives to highlight key considerations as the country progresses in this new ecology era.
documents.author: Shin, D.H.;Choi, M.J.;

documents.title: Actualizing big data analytics affordances: A revelatory case study
documents.abstract:
Abstract

Drawing on a revelatory case study, we identify four big data analytics (BDA) actualization mechanisms: (1) enhancing, (2) constructing, (3) coordinating, and (4) integrating, which manifest in actions on three socio-technical system levels, i.e., the structure, actor, and technology levels. We investigate the actualization of four BDA affordances at an automotive manufacturing company, i.e., establishing customer-centric marketing, provisioning vehicle-data-driven services, data-driven vehicle developing, and optimizing production processes. This study introduces a theoretical perspective to BDA research that explains how organizational actions contribute to actualizing BDA affordances. We further provide practical implications that can help guide practitioners in BDA adoption.
documents.author: Dremel, Christian;Herterich, Matthias M.;Wulf, Jochen;vom Brocke, Jan;

documents.title: “If they don’t tell us what they do with it, why would we trust them?” Trust, transparency and benefit-sharing in Smart Farming
documents.abstract:
Abstract

Advances in Smart Farming and Big Data applications have the potential to help agricultural industries meet productivity and sustainability challenges. However, these benefits are unlikely to be realised if the social implications of these technological innovations are not adequately considered by those who promote them. Big Data applications are intrinsically socio-technical; their development and deployment are a product of social interactions between people, institutional and regulatory settings, as well as the technology itself. This paper explores the socio-technical factors and conditions that influence the development of Smart Farming and Big Data applications, using a multi-level perspective on transitions combined with social practice theory. We conducted semi-structured interviews with 26 Australian grain farmers and industry stakeholders to elicit their perspectives on benefits and risks of these changes. The analysis shows that issues related to trust are central concerns for many participants. These include procedural concerns about transparency and distributional concerns about who will benefit from access to and use of “farmers’ data”. These concerns create scepticism about the value of ‘smart’ technologies amongst some industry stakeholders, especially farmers. It also points to a divergence of expectations and norms between actors and institutions at the regime and niche levels in the emerging transition towards Smart Farming. Bridging this divide will require niche level interventions to enhance the agency of farmers and their local networks in these transactions, and, the cooperative design of new institutions at regime level to facilitate the fair and transparent allocation of risk and benefit in farming data information chains.

Highlights

  • Australian grains industry stakeholders can see a range of benefits associated with smart farming.
  • Current limitations of Australia’s digital infrastructure are constraining smart farming.
  • Some farmers are sceptical about who benefits from smart farming technologies.
  • A lack of trust and transparency surrounding data ownership could also limit smart farming.

documents.title: 행위자-네트워크 이론을 통한 태권도 미디어 산업의 변천과정 탐색
documents.abstract: 태권도 미디어 산업은 다양한 행위자들이 네트워크를 형성하며 복잡한 상호작용을 통해 발전하고 있는 시장으로, 구조를 체계적으로 이해하고 분석할 필요성이 제기된다. 특히 태권도는 미디어와의 결합을 통해 다양한 산업으로 확장되며 발전해왔고, 이러한 과정에서 행위자-네트워크 이론을 통해 인간뿐만 아니라 기술과 사물 같은 비인간 행위자도 행위자로 간주하며, 모든 존재가 네트워크 속에서 관계를 통해 표현된다는 점에서 사회적 현상을 보다 체계적으로 분석하는데 도움을 준다. &#xD; 이에 본 연구는 태권도 미디어 산업의 변천과정을 행위자-네트워크 이론의 관점에서 탐색하고자 하였다. 이를 위해 시기별로 나타나는 태권도 미디어 산업의 현황을 빅데이터 분석을 통해 파악하고, 그 안에 포함된 다양한 대상들과 이들 간의 관계를 분석하여 ‘행위자’, ‘네트워크’, 그리고 ‘중간역할’을 규명하고자 하였다. 주요 키워드 간 관계 분석을 통해 복잡한 사회적 현상을 보다 체계적이고 객관적으로 이해할 수 있었으며, 태권도 미디어 산업의 발전 과정을 이해하는 데 있어 중요한 자료를 제공하고자 하였다. 또한, 이러한 분석 결과를 바탕으로 태권도 미디어 산업과 같은 복합적 네트워크가 시기별로 어떻게 변화하고 형성되었는지를 번역의 관점에서 규명하고자 하였다. 이러한 연구목적을 달성하기 위해 첫째, 시기별로 나타나는 태권도 미디어 산업의 현황은 어떠한가? 둘째, 시기별 태권도 미디어 산업의 행위자, 네트워크, 중간역할은 어떠한가? 셋째, 번역의 관점에서 바라본 시기별 태권도 미디어 산업의 변천과정은 어떠한가? 라는 연구문제를 설정하였으며, 다음과 같은 결론을 도출하였다.&#xD; 먼저, 시기별 태권도 미디어 산업의 현황을 탐색하기 위해 1990년을 기점으로 본 연구 시점까지의 기간에 대해 10년을 주기로 총 4개의 구간으로 나누어 ‘태권도+미디어’ 키워드를 중심으로 빅데이터 분석을 실시하였다. 빅데이터 분석결과, 1990년대(1990년-1999년)에서 나타나는 주요 키워드는 태권도, 미디어, 세계, 대회, 신문 등으로 나타났으며, CONCOR 분석결과로는 태권도 인지도 표상, 태권도 국제화, 생활스포츠, 태권도 문화정책의 네가지 군집으로 범주화 되었다. 이에 대한 행위자, 네트워크, 중간역할을 도출해 본 결과, 태권도 인지도 표상 군집에서 행위자로는 국기원, 단증, 관장, 도장, 뉴스, 기자 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 행정 전산화, 태권도 대중화 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 컴퓨터, 뉴스, 신문 등이 도출되었다. 태권도 국제화 군집에서 행위자로는 선수, 연맹, 위원장, 대회, 태권도, 올림픽 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 올림픽 정식종목, 태권도 국제화 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 TV중계, 뉴스 등이 도출되었다. 생활스포츠 군집에서 행위자로는 건강, 스포츠, 운동 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 생활스포츠화 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 뉴스, 신문 등이 도출되었다. 태권도 문화정책 군집에서 행위자로는 축제, 개발, 정책, 관광 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 문화 자원화, 지역경제 활성화 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 신문, 광고 홍보 등이 도출되었다. &#xD; 2000년대(2000년-2009년)에서 나타나는 주요 키워드는 태권도, 미디어, 대학교, 태권도학과, 대회 등으로 나타났으며, CONCOR 분석결과로는 태권도 교육의 사회적 기능, 태권도 영상매체, 태권도와 미디어, 올림픽 정식종목의 네가지 군집으로 범주화 되었다. 이에 대한 행위자, 네트워크, 중간역할을 도출해 본 결과, 태권도 교육의 사회적 기능 군집에서 행위자로는 학생, 대학교, 태권도학과, 수능, 수시 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 교육커리큘럼, 대입 제도 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 온라인 원서 접수 등이 도출되었다. 태권도 영상매체 군집에서 행위자로는 영화, 영상, 온라인, 문화, 교육 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 UCC 공모전, 태권도 영화 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 태권도 영상 콘텐츠, 멀티미디어 등이 도출되었다. 태권도와 미디어 군집에서 행위자로는 사범, 도장, 디지털, 대회, 인터넷신문 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 정보공유 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 디지털 미디어, 인터넷 기사 등이 도출되었다. 올림픽 정식종목 군집에서 행위자로는 올림픽, 기사, 선수, 금메달 등이 있으며, 네트워크로는 올림픽 정식종목, 경기력, 세계화 등이 있다. 중간역할로는 올림픽 경기 중계, 경기 내용 전달 매체 등이 도출되었다. &#xD; 2010년대(2010년-2019년)에서 나타나는 주요 키워드는 태권도, 미디어, 대학교, 태권도학과, 대회 등으로 나타났으며, CONCOR 분석결과로는 태권도와 문화콘텐츠, 태권도 문화콘텐츠 확장, 입시의 다변화, 태권도 위상 강화의 네가지 군집으로 범주화 되었다. 이에 대한 행위자, 네트워크, 중간역할을 도출해 본 결과, 태권도와 문화콘텐츠 군집에서 행위자로는 시범, 축제, 체험, 공연, 글로벌, 퍼포먼스 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 한류 콘텐츠, 태권도 인지도 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 태권도 홍보 방송, 소셜미디어 등이 도출되었다. 태권도 문화콘텐츠 확장 군집에서 행위자로는 콘텐츠, 예술, 교육, 영상, 관광, 스포츠, 디지털 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 미디어 플랫폼, 문화 자원 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 교육 및 관광 관련 디지털 콘텐츠 등이 도출되었다. 입시의 다변화 군집에서 행위자로는 학생, 수시, 태권도학과, 대학교 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 대입 실기 전형 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 시범 영상 콘텐츠, 소셜미디어 등이 도출되었다. 태권도 위상 강화 군집에서 행위자로는 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 태권도 경기화, 공정성, 세계화 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 태권도의 전 세계 중계, 전자호구 시스템 등이 도출되었다. &#xD; 2020년대(2020년-2024년)에서 나타나는 주요 키워드는 태권도, 미디어, 대학교, 대회, 선수 등으로 나타났으며, CONCOR 분석결과로는 소셜미디어 기능 강화, 팬데믹에 의한 문화 변동, 태권도 교육의 사회변동의 세가지 군집으로 범주화 되었다. 이에 대한 행위자, 네트워크, 중간역할을 도출해 본 결과, 소셜미디어 기능 강화 군집에서 행위자로는 소셜미디어, 영상, 시범, 공연, 퍼포먼스 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 태권도 콘텐츠, 인지도 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 소셜미디어, 유튜브, 기타 소셜미디어 등이 도출되었다. 팬데믹에 의한 문화 변동 군집에서 행위자로는 코로나19, 온라인, 대회, 선수, 품새, 사범 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 온라인 대회, 비대면 시스템, 디지털 콘텐츠 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 비대면 대회 운영, 온라인 품새 및 시범 확대, 디지털 전환 촉진 등이 도출되었다. 태권도 교육의 사회변동 군집에서 행위자로는 입시, 태권도, 경쟁, 대학교 등이 있고, 네트워크로는 대입 제도, 시범대회, 품새대회 등이 있으며, 중간역할로는 실기 평가 강화, 입시 경쟁 촉진, 공정성 향상 등이 도출되었다. &#xD; 이러한 분석을 바탕으로 1990년대부터 2024년까지 태권도 미디어 산업의 변천 과정은 각 시기의 기술적 발전과 사회적 변화에 맞추어 다양한 형태로 진화해 왔음을 알 수 있었다. 이에 행위자-네트워크 이론의 번역 개념을 적용하여 변화를 분석해보면, 미디어는 태권도 산업 내에서 단순히 정보를 전달하는 수단을 넘어, 미디어 산업의 발전과 태권도의 글로벌 확장을 이끄는 중요한 행위자로서 기능해 왔음을 확인할 수 있다. 먼저, 1990년대는 태권도와 디지털 미디어가 서로를 향해 문을 열기 시작한 도입의 시기로, 태권도는 생활 스포츠와 국제 스포츠로 자리 잡기 위한 초석을 마련하였으며, 1991년 세계적 웹 기술인 WWW의 등장으로 인터넷 미디어가 발달하며 대중과의 접근성이 크게 높아졌다. 태권도는 디지털 환경을 통해 효과적으로 대중에게 다가갈 수 있었고, 국기원은 단증 발급 및 관리 시스템의 전산화를 통해 행정의 효율성을 높이며 신뢰성을 강화하였다. 또한, 태권도가 올림픽 시범 종목으로 선정되면서 TV 중계를 통한 국제적 인지도가 크게 확대되었고, 이는 태권도의 대중화와 국제화 과정에서 미디어가 필수적인 중개자 역할을 수행했음을 보여준다. 2000년대는 태권도가 디지털 미디어의 확산과 함께 본격적으로 전개된 시기로, 인터넷 사용이 보편화됨에 따라 태권도 관련 콘텐츠의 전파가 더욱 용이해졌다. 이 시기에 태권도는 다양한 대학에 태권도학과가 설립되며 교육적 기능이 사회적 관심사로 부각되었고, 이는 미디어를 통한 홍보와 대중화의 결과였다. 또한, UCC와 같은 새로운 미디어 형식은 젊은 층의 관심을 끌며 태권도를 대중적인 문화 콘텐츠로 변화시켰다. 태권도가 올림픽 정식 종목으로 채택되면서 국제적 위상이 강화되었고, 미디어는 경기의 공정성을 높이고 관중의 흥미를 증대시키는 데 중요한 역할을 했다. 2010년대는 태권도가 한류와 결합하여 글로벌 문화 콘텐츠로 자리 잡은 확장의 시기였다. 스마트폰의 대중화와 소셜미디어의 확산은 태권도의 시범, 공연, 축제 등 다양한 콘텐츠가 전 세계로 빠르게 확산될 수 있도록 하였다. 특히, 입시제도의 변화로 실기 중심의 태권도 입시 콘텐츠가 인기를 끌며 젊은 세대의 관심을 새롭게 유도하였다. 국제 대회와 아시안게임에서 품새 종목이 정식 채택되면서 태권도의 경기적 다양성과 문화적 가치가 동시에 확장되었고, 이는 디지털 플랫폼과 소셜미디어를 통해 더욱 부각되었다. 2020년대는 팬데믹이라는 예기치 못한 상황 속에서 태권도가 디지털 기술을 적극적으로 응용하며 대중과의 연결을 유지한 응용의 시기로 볼 수 있다. 코로나19로 인해 온라인 대회와 비대면 훈련 시스템이 도입되었고, VR과 AR 기술을 활용한 체험형 콘텐츠가 개발되면서 더욱 몰입감 있는 디지털 경험이 가능해졌다. 실기 평가와 대회가 비대면으로 전환되면서 온라인 플랫폼은 실시간 중계와 대중의 참여를 이끄는 중요한 통로로 자리 잡았다. 이러한 기술적 진보는 태권도가 디지털 콘텐츠로서의 기능을 강화하며 팬데믹 상황에서도 대중과 지속적으로 연결될 수 있도록 했다.&#xD; 결론적으로, 태권도 미디어 산업은 도입, 전개, 확장, 응용의 변천 과정을 거쳐온 것을 확인할 수 있었다. 1990년대에는 미디어와의 첫 연결을 통해 태권도의 대중적 가능성을 도입하였고, 2000년대에는 디지털 미디어의 발전을 바탕으로 교육적, 사회적 기능을 강화하였다. 2010년대에는 한류와 결합하여 글로벌 문화 콘텐츠로 확장되었으며, 2020년대에는 디지털 기술을 통해 비대면 환경에서도 대중과의 연결을 유지하였다. 이러한 변천 과정을 통해 미디어는 태권도 산업의 핵심 행위자로서 네트워크를 형성하고 확장하며, 태권도가 글로벌 스포츠이자 문화 콘텐츠로 자리매김하는 데 중요한 역할을 했음을 알 수 있다. 태권도 미디어 산업의 발전은 시대적 요구와 기술적 변화에 맞춰 미디어가 지속적으로 그 역할을 조정해 온 결과라 할 수 있다.

documents.title: 개인정보이동권에 관한 공법적 연구
documents.abstract: 기술 중심의 디지털 사회 초기에는 개인정보주체에게 개인정보처리에 관한 수동적이고 방어적인 개인정보보호권만이 인정되었다. 하지만 인간 중심의 디지털 사회로 전환되고, 모든 일상생활이 디지털 사회 안에서 이루어지는 디지털 전환(Digital Transformation) 사회로 디지털 사회의 고도화되고 있다. 현 시점에서 개인정보주체는 더 이상 개인정보처리의 수동적인 객체가 아니다. 개인정보이동권(right to data portability)을 통하여 개인정보주체는 자율적이고 주체적인 의사에 따라 관리 및 활용이 가능하게 되었고, 필요에 따라 개인정보를 전송시켜 온라인 플랫폼이 달라지더라도 자신의 사회적 인격상(타인에 비칠 자신의 모습)을 일치시킬 수 있고, 개인정보주체의 기호(嗜好), 노하우, 추억 등이 집적된 자신만의 스토리를 그대로 제3의 온라인 플랫폼으로 ‘연결’시킴으로 인하여 디지털 라이프의 연속성을 유지할 수 있게 되었다. &#xD; 또한 개인정보이동권은 경쟁 기업으로 개인정보를 전송하게 하여 경쟁을 촉진하는 원동력이 되어, 구글, 페이스북 등 소수 미국 중심의 거대 온라인 플랫폼 사업자들의 독과점 시장을 해체시킬 수 있는 효과도 기대할 수 있다. 그리고 흩어져있는 개인정보를 한 플랫폼으로 모아 통합·관리하여 맞춤형 서비스를 받을 수 있는 마이데이터(MyData) 서비스의 법적 근거이기도 하다. &#xD; 이러한 실익으로 인하여 미국, 캐나다 등 세계의 주요 국가에서 개인정보이동권을 이미 규정하였거나 개정안을 준비 중에 있다. 따라서 우리나라에서도 개인정보이동권이 활성화될 수 있는 법·정책적 방안을 제언하고자 한다. 이를 위하여 개인정보이동권의 본질과 해외 동향, 개인정보이동권의 국내 도입과 법적 쟁점에 대하여 상세하여 분석하였다. 개인정보 보호법제 역사의 개괄, 개인정보 보호의 기본 원칙, 개인정보 보호법제의 패러다임의 변화, 새로운 권리로서의 개인정보이동권의 등장 배경과 기능, 개인정보이동권에 관한 해외의 법제 동향, 개인정보이동권의 의의와 법적 성격, 개인정보이동권과 열람권과의 관계, 개인정보이동권의 규정 도입에 관한 찬·반론과 실익, 개인정보이동권의 일반법에의 도입 논의 그리고 도입과 관련한 주요 쟁점을 검토하였다. 이러한 연구 결과 개인정보이동권의 입법 방향은 개인정보 보호법제의 국제적 정합성 도모의 필요성을 위하여 유럽연합과 유사한 규정을 마련해야 국경이 없는 디지털 전환 사회 안에서 국제적 혼란을 막을 수 있을 것이라는 결론을 도출하였다. 또한 국내적 정합성을 도모하기 위하여 일반법인 「개인정보 보호법」에 규정하고 개인정보 보호위원회에서 일원화하여 감독할 것을 제시하였다. 마지막으로 개인정보주체의 권리를 강화하기 위한 방안으로 국제 표준 수준의 프라이버시 보호 제공을 위한 방안, 본래 의미의 개인정보이동권 보장을 위한 방안, 마이데이터 서비스의 경우에는 ‘알고 하는 동의’를 실행할 수 있는 방안을 제시하였다.

documents.title: 치유 개념을 적용한 실버타운 환경 디자인 연구
documents.abstract: 국문요약&#xD; 국민 경제가 발전하면서 삶의 질에 대한 사람들의 기준도 점점 더 높아지고 있다. 하지만 현재 일부 노인 돌봄 환경, 특히 60세 이상 노인을 대상으로 한 노인 돌봄 환경은 노인의 생리적, 정신적 수요를 만족시키지 못하고 있다. 노인 돌봄 구조의 변화로 인해 일부 노인은 집에서 노후를 보내지 못하고, 실버타운에 입주하기도 한다. 사별하거나, 병환으로 고생하거나, 거동이 불편해 개인적〮사회적 스트레스를 받는 노인에게 심신 건강과 스트레스 해소 및 치유 기능이 갖춰진 돌봄 환경이 필요하다. 또한 노인의 심신 건강을 치유해 줄 수 있는 환경을 조성해 주는 것은 사회의 조화로운 발전에도 중요하다. 노인 돌봄 공간에 원예치료 환경을 조성하면 시설 미관에 도움이 될 뿐만 아니라 심신 건강에 대한 노인의 수요도 만족시켜 노인이 여생을 더 즐겁게 보낼 수 있다.&#xD; 관련 문헌 연구를 보면, 현재 노인 돌봄 환경 문제에 대한 연구는 주로 건축 계획 분야에 집중되어 있으며, 노인 돌봄 환경 문제에 대한 연구는 비교적 적은 편이다. 연구는 대개 기술적 측면에 치중되어 있는데, 주로 어떻게 하면 건축과 개조를 통해 노인에게 편안한 거주 환경을 제공할 수 있는지에 대해 고찰하였다. 본 논문은 인구 고령화가 점차 심각해지고 사회 노인 돌봄 서비스 시스템이 구축되는 과정에서 실버타운의 수요 측면의 문제점을 깊이 있게 연구하여 노인을 위한 더 나은 노인 돌봄 환경을 만들고자 한다．&#xD; 전 세계적으로 노인 인구가 증가하면서 실버타운에 대한 사회적 관심이 늘어나고 있으며, 이에 따라 돌봄 산업도 빠르게 발전하고 있다. 또한 의료의 발달과 삶의 수준 향상 및 노인의 노후 삶에 대한 인식 변화로 인하여, 단순하고 제한적인 노인 돌봄 환경은 노인들의 정신 및 생활에 대한 수요를 만족시킬 수 없다. 동시에 치유 개념에 대한 연구가 많이 이루어지면서 사람들은 식물이 인간의 생리적 기능 및 심리와 깊은 관련이 있다는 것을 점차 인식하기 시작했으며, 이에 원예치료도 다시 각광받기 시작했다. 치유 개념을 실버타운에 적용하면 실버타운의 수준을 높일 수 있고, 노인에게 보다 다양한 노후 생활을 제공해 줄 수 있다. 동서양의 치유 이념과 실버타운 환경에 관한 연구를 통해 치유 개념의 기존 연구와 실제 적용에 문제가 있다는 것을 발견하였다. 첫째, 중국이 실버타운의 치유 환경 연구를 뒤늦게 시작하여 기존의 연구 성과가 적은 편이며 치유 개념과 실버타운을 결합시킨 연구가 집중적으로 이루어지지 못하였다. 따라서 본 논문을 통해 치유 개념을 환경 디자인에 적용할 방법을 모색하고 종합∙귀납하여 중국의 실버타운 환경 디자인에 도움이 되고자 한다. 둘째, 본 논문에서는 주로 동서양 국가에서 대표 사례를 선정하여 분석하였다. 구미 국가는 실버타운을 비교적 일찍 건설하기 시작하였으며 디자인도 충분히 성숙한 단계에 진입했다. 그에 반해 중국은 한 발 늦게 실버타운을 건설하기 시작했으며 국내 성공 사례가 부족하여 실외 환경 디자인 및 무장애 디자인 등 분야에서 참고할 만한 사례를 찾기 어려웠다. 따라서 본 논문에서 사례로 제시한 중국 베이징 동방 태양성 실버타운은 주로 해외 성공 경험을 참고하여 건설한 것이며 여전히 미흡한 점이 많다. (사례 분석에서 자세히 설명)&#xD; 본 논문의 환경 디자인은 실외 환경 디자인, 조명, 색채, 식물, 공간 계획 등을 포함하며 실내 환경 디자인은 제외한다.　또한 치유 개념과 실버타운 환경 디자인 관련 문헌 수집과 분석을 통해 동서양의 치유 개념 적용 및 실버타운 현황을 알아보고 실버타운 환경 디자인에 존재하는 문제점을 종합하여 본 과제의 연구 방향과 주제 의식을 확립하였다. 본 논문은 노인의 각기 다른 수요에서 출발해 실버타운 디자인에 적합한 요건을 파악하고, 치유 개념을 실버타운에 적용하는 방법에 대해 분석하여 실행 가능하고 적절한 실버타운의 환경 디자인 방법을 도출하였다. 본 논문의 주요 연구 성과는 실버타운의 환경 디자인을 분석하고 치유 개념 적용 방식 결합하여 실버타운 환경 디자인에 치유 개념을 적용하는 방법을 도출하였으며, 치유 개념을 합리적으로 활용한 디자인 방법과 현지 문화경관, 향토 식물자원을 활용해 편안하고 건강한 돌봄 환경을 조성하는 데에 있다. 이러한 방법을 실버타운에 적용해 식물, 지형, 도로포장, 물, 소품 표지에 활용되는 방법을 도출하여 실버타운의 다양한 실외 환경을 위한 구체적인 디자인 방법을 제시하였으며, 이는 보다 과학적이고 합리적인 실버타운 환경 조성에 도움이 된다.&#xD; 상기 서술한 내용을 기반으로 본 논문에서는 실버타운 치유환경 계획의 기초적인 영향 요인을 결합하고, 노인의 수요와 선호를 참고하여 실버타운 치유환경에 대한 체계적 연구를 실시하고, 연구 성과에 대한 이론적 분석을 통해 실버타운 치유환경 계획에 대한 디자인 전략을 제시하였으며 주요 내용은 다음과 같다. &#xD; (1) 실버타운 및 치유 환경 관련 이론과 동서양의 기존 연구 성과를 정리하고 연구와 관련된 개념 및 범위를 정하였다. 본 논문에서는 치유 환경 디자인 개념을 다음과 같이 정했다. 노인의 실버타운 환경에 대한 수요를 근거로 일정한 디자인 방법을 사용하여 노인의 신체 건강을 촉진하는 건강한 지역사회 환경을 구축하는 것이다. &#xD; (2) 노인의 행동 및 선호, 심리 및 생리적 특징 차원에서 출발하여 실버타운 치유 환경의 영향요소 및 디자인 원칙의 다양성을 분석하였으며, 실버타운 내 치유 환경 디자인은 안전성, 다양성, 현지성, 적극성, 그리고 교화 역할 등의 원칙을 기준으로 노인의 ‘즐거운 노후, 안정적 노후’에 대한 수요를 만족시켜야 한다. 기존 연구를 통해, 실버타운의 정원 치유환경 계획의 목표를 분석하여, 실버타운의 치유 환경 디자인 요소 간의 연계 및 영향을 종합하였다. 실버타운 환경의 치유 개념 적용을 더욱 자세하게 설명하기 위하여, 본 논문은 동서양의 비교적 대표성을 지닌 몇 가지 실버타운 사례를 분석하였으며, 중국 베이징(北京) 동방태양성(东方太阳城)의 실버타운 환경 디자인을 주요 연구 대상으로 삼고 상기 연구 내용과 결합하여 중국의 치유 개념에 적합한 실버타운 환경 디자인 이론을 도출했다. 베이징 동방태양성을 위한 실버타운 환경계획 디자인 제안 및 방법을 제시하여 향후 치유 환경을 실버타운 내에 조성할 수 있도록 과학적이고 효과적인 이론과 참고 근거를 제공하였다.&#xD; (3) 치유 환경 디자인의 역동성, 전체성, 연관성을 통해 실버타운 치유 환경에 대해 체계적으로 연구하고, 참고 문헌, 기존 연구 성과 등을 결합하여 실버타운 치유 환경 디자인 요소 체계를 구축하였다.&#xD; &#xD; 치유 개념을 기반으로 한 실버타운 환경 디자인은 노인 감각기관의 충분한 자극, 자연 공간의 쾌적함 강화, 다양한 식물 선택, 활동 공간의 안전성 등을 고려해야 하며, 식물 등 여러 조건을 충분히 활용하여 인체에 대한 자연환경의 치유 기능을 제고하고 이를 통해 노인의 신체적·심리적 회복을 도모해야 한다. 실버타운 환경의 구역 요소와 지역문화 요소 등을 결합하여 최종적으로 실버타운 환경 디자인에 치유 개념을 적용할 때의 구체적인 디자인 요구사항 및 응용 방법을 도출해냈다. 구체적인 내용은 다음과 같다. &#xD; 실버타운 치유 환경 디자인 요소의 다양화는 노인들의 산책, 명상, 신선한 공기 호흡 등의 활동 수요를 만족시킨다. 실버타운 치유 환경 디자인 요소는 현지성, 적극성 및 교화 등의 원칙에 따라‘노인이 새로운 것을 배우고 즐거움을 얻는다. (老有所乐， 老有所学)’심리를 만족시켜야 한다. 또한 시설 내부 및 주변 공기 질, 토양 환경, 물, 교통 편의성 등의 요소도 실버타운 치유 환경 디자인에 대한 노인의 만족도와 사용에 영향을 미치는 것을 발견했다. 첫째, 실버타운의 환경과 분위기. 미학적 특징의 경우, 시설의 전체적인 색의 조화, 공간의 크기와 환경의 쾌적함, 식물의 계절적 변화와 레이어 등을 중시해야 한다. 문화성의 경우, 일정한 지역 문화를 구현하고, 타운 내 문화 발전에 힘써야 한다. 생태성의 경우, 좋은 식물 군락과 합리적인 식물을 재배하고, 경관 환경 요소와 식물을 합리적으로 배치해야 한다. 식물을 선택할 때 반드시 실버타운의 입지를 고려하여 남부 식물 혹은 북부 식물을 심을 것인지 결정해야 하며, 식물의 오감기능을 중시하여 교목, 관목, 화훼, 지피류 등 다양한 식물 종류를 선택해야 한다. 구체적으로는 노인의 신체재활에 도움을 주는 식물이어야 하며, 식물 색을 배합할 때 계절감이 비교적 뚜렷한 식물을 선택해야 하지만 침엽수, 버들개지 및 독성이 있는 식물은 사용해서는 안 되며 노인의 신체 건강을 위한 식물을 선택하는 것을 전제로 해야 한다.　둘째, 실버타운의 공간 배치. 교통의 접근 용이성의 경우, 안전하고 편리한 도로 체계를 갖춰야 한다. 공간 인식 용이성의 경우, 명확한 표지와 공간 디자인을 사용해 간결하고 명확한 공간 배치를 해야 한다. 셋째, 실버타운의 공간 조성. 공간 적응성의 경우, 노인의 다양한 활동 등 수요를 만족시켜야 한다. 참여성의 경우, 다양한 노인의 개성과 수요를 중시하고, 단순하고 쉽게 조작할 수 있는 시설 등을 조성해야 한다. 공간 영역으로는 다층적인 공간 등을 디자인해야 한다. 넷째 실버타운의 인성화 디자인: 안전성의 경우, 완벽한 예방 보호조치를 취하여 디자인에 존재하는 안전 문제 등을 없애야 한다. 무장애 디자인의 경우, 실버타운 내 도로의 무장애 통행 등에 신경 써야 한다.&#xD; 마지막으로, 이번 연구는 미비한 점이 많으며, 앞으로의 학습 및 연구를 통해 좀 더 심층적인 탐색이 필요하다. &#xD; 키워드: 치유, 실버타운, 환경 디자인&#xD;

documents.title: 빅데이터 시대에 개인화서비스와 프라이버시 패러독스의 고찰 -사회기술적 관점을 중심으로-
documents.abstract: This study looks upon big data as ‘Socio-Technical Systems’ that has a big benefit but also big risk. And Itassumes that the big data as Socio-Technical Systems has an embedded paradox and fundamental complexity.That is, Big Data has a paradoxical complexity which is high-value of personalization vs high-cost with aprivacy concerns. So, this study aims to consider those complexity. It considers it from ‘SociotechnicalPerspective’ approach which analyzes external environment, internal environment and major issues. As a results,it is necessary to obtain trust and also relevant procedural fairness for it. Especially, for finding a way to makea procedural fairness, it suggests that it has to development the context approach frame continuously.
